name: Dumbbell deadlift
summary: Weights on the floor beside the feet; hinge and bend to grip them, then stand tall by driving the floor away.
setup: Stand side-on to the phone, weights beside the feet. Push the hips back and bend the knees to reach the weights with a flat back, then stand by driving the legs and hips together. Lower the same way.
brief: Stand with the weights beside the feet. Push the hips back and bend the knees to reach them with a flat back, then stand by driving the legs and hips together.
why: From the side the trunk hinges and returns each rep, and the back folding further than the hips — the sign of a rounded pull — shows as the trunk angle dropping too far.
regression: Weights on a low step; kettlebell between the feet.
contraindications: Lower back pain; unable to keep a flat back at the bottom.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Back rounding
faults.tip: Brace, chest proud, and lift the weights from a higher surface if the back rounds.

faults.label: Rounding at the bottom
faults.tip: If the back rounds to reach the floor, start from a raised surface instead.

faults.label: Hips shooting up first
faults.tip: The shoulders and hips rise at the same rate; if the hips lead, the back finishes the lift.

faults.label: Jerking off the floor
faults.tip: Pull the tension on first, then stand. A jerk loads the back before it is braced.

guide.cannotSee: The back rounding under a shirt.

points.t: Hinges with a flat back; stands fully tall.
Knees bend enough to reach the weights; heels down.
